britannica-1911-ten-kate-jan-jacob-lodew:
Jan Jacob Lodewijk ten Kate, a Dutch church man and poet, gets a verse life in the 1911 Britannica. Born at The Hague in eighteen nineteen, he first worked as a law clerk. A friend saw the gift of verse in him and sent him to school for the church. He read church lore at Utrecht from eighteen thirty eight to forty three. Then he served as pastor at towns of his land in turn.

Prose and verse poured from his pen through all those years. Travel books of the Rhine and of Italy stand among his prose works. His long poems of high fame treat the made world, the stars, and the year round. No peer matched his gift of turn verse from far tongues to Dutch. He turned works from Dante to Longfellow in clear sweet Dutch lines.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-heeswijk:
Holland's Abbey of Berne at Heeswijk rose from confiscation to new life through stubborn continuity. Founded in 1134 by Fulcold, Lord of Teisterband, who turned his castle into an abbey after a vow in battle, Berne won privileges from Holland's counts and Brabant's dukes. It held patronage over nine parishes.

Calvinists plundered it in 1572 and 1579, and by 1648 all its lands were confiscated, yet hidden priests kept the faith in North Brabant and Gelderland, abbots were elected without break. The community rented Heeswijk late in the seventeenth century and bought it in 1786. Abbot Neefs restored common life in 1847, a college opened in 1889, and priests sent to Wisconsin in 1895 built St. Norbert's College at De Pere and wiped out the Vilatte schism.

OpenAI chief Sam Altman talks with Joe Rogan in episode 2044 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Altman led the company behind ChatGPT through its explosive rise and a boardroom coup that briefly removed him. The man behind the machine speaks carefully in this corporate hour.

Altman explains how he sees AI changing work, science, and daily life in the coming years. He addresses safety fears and the question of who should control such power. Rogan presses him on risks in plain terms a lay audience can follow. Tech-curious and cautious listeners get the revolution's most powerful figure in his own words.
